about: The one row-kind classification (CONTEXT.md "row kind"): what a scene inventory row's objects do in their scene, worked out free from the reading's own words, never from a model call or a record per scene (score/stages/row_kinds.py). A row's kind is the first kind, in this file's order, whose `nouns` hold its reading noun whole (the reading's head noun, the row's `noun`: a "floor plate" is no plate); only a row read with no noun is matched by its name's last word. A kind says what its objects do (`does`): emits (a particle effect of data/effects/kinds.json, `effects`, made by the effects stage), moves (a rigid move of the motion stage, `motion`: its kind in data/checks/motion.json with the cited speeds, and how it moves, or why it stands), loose (free to fall and be pushed: the physics trial drops or pushes it), glows (a lamp: the light layer's), shows (a screen) and grows (a plant: the crops layer's). The `kind` field of a row (code or generate) is how it is made, not this. Every entry is general: a word, never a scene's name.

motion.why: a door swings a right angle open on the hinge at its own left edge and shuts again
a crane slews a right angle about its own middle and back
a fan turns steadily about its own middle
a vehicle drives along free lanes, which a plan does not hold: it stands parked where the plan lays it
a lift's travel needs the height it serves, which a plan does not hold: it stands lowered where the plan lays it
